title: Molten Streaking for Singles: Rapid Tube-Free Serial Purification of Viruses
author: Kathryn Kauffman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.j8pcrvn
materials: Equilibrate the top agar to 50-52°C: Place the beaker-waterbath with the top agar onto a hot plate with stirring, place a thermometer into the beaker-waterbath and leave it there to wait for equilibration to 50-53°C (Figure 1). a Note: This will require setting the heat block to a temperature greater than the target temperature, for example up to 85°C, but this is dependent on specific heat block models and must be determined by the user.
Prepare the molten agar overlay: Have all materials ready to advance to Streak 1 steps (Steps 5, 6, 7, & 8) before starting this step as the lawn cannot be allowed to solidify before the streak.

steps.title: Prepare beaker-waterbath
steps.instruction: Place a bottle of top agar into a glass beaker and add water to the beaker up to the level of the top agar in the bottle (e.g., a 500mL glass bottle into a 1L beaker).

steps.title: Melt the top agar
steps.instruction: Melt the top agar in a microwave using a beaker-waterbath, ensuring a 'smooth melt' to allow plaque visibility and preventing boil-over.

substeps.instruction: Melt top agar for several 5-minute cycles at low % power until nearly completely melted.
Increase % power and cook until the top agar comes to a boil.
Bring the top agar to a boil 3 times, observing closely to prevent boil-over.

steps.title: Add host to bottom agar
steps.instruction: Pipette 100uL of overnight host culture directly onto the bottom agar.

steps.title: Apply molten top agar
steps.instruction: Pipette 2mL of molten top agar from the bottle directly to the bottom agar next to the hosts using a 5mL or serological pipette.

steps.title: Create overlay
steps.instruction: Swirl the plate vigorously but briefly to mix the bacteria and molten top agar, then spread it across the plate.

steps.title: Streak viruses into molten agar
steps.instruction: Swiftly streak viruses from the source into the still-molten top agar before it solidifies to ensure single colonies form in the host lawn.

substeps.instruction: If using liquid stock: drop up to 20 ul of sample into one spot in the molten overlay.
If using frozen stock: collect a small mass with a sterile toothpick/tip, transfer to one spot, and keep the stock frozen during the procedure.
If using a plaque: insert a sterile toothpick into the source plaque.
Swirl the first toothpick into a small area of the molten agar overlay.
Use a second toothpick to make three separate strokes in the same direction, passing through the area touched by the first toothpick each time.
Use a third toothpick to make a repeating Z-stroke, passing once through the streaks from the second toothpick.

steps.title: Solidify and incubate
steps.instruction: Leave the plate on the bench, top agar side up, for 20 minutes to allow the agar to completely solidify.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate in desired incubation conditions and monitor for plaque formation.
Protect plates from desiccation if monitoring for extended periods (days or weeks).

steps.title: Perform serial purification
steps.instruction: Repeat the streaking process using a single, well-separated plaque from the first plate as the source for the desired number of purifications.

substeps.instruction: Insert a sterile toothpick into a single plaque and repeat the streaking for singles approach.
Pick and archive single plaques from the final streak, or use them to generate large-scale liquid or plate lysates.
